-- | Bounded logical admission, separate from physical process ownership.
--
-- Create a t'Scheduler' with 'newScheduler', 'admit' an operation, then
-- dispatch with 'claim'. 'status' separates observed progress, the first
-- caller outcome and retained responsibility. Cancellation of 'await' does
-- not release admission. 'connectionRetired' also retains uncertain work.
--
-- This component performs no tmux IO and proves no external completion.
-- The Runtime must supply evidence to 'finish' or 'refuseBeforeBirth', and
-- protect physical-child and byte capacity for inspection too. The logical
-- reserve here does not reserve those resources.
module LibTmux.Internal.Scheduler
  ( -- * Context and admission
    Scheduler, Operation, Lane (..), newScheduler, admit, claim
    -- * Ownership groups
  , Group, newGroup, admitIn, outstandingIn, memberOf
    -- * Detached observations
  , Stage (..), Outcome (..), Status (..), status, await, outstanding
    -- * Evidence and uncertainty
  , Completion (..), markDispatched, markResponseClosed, finish, markUnknown
  , cancelQueued, refuseBeforeBirth, connectionRetired, detachResponsibility
    -- * Shutdown and errors
  , closeAdmission, AdmissionError (..)
  ) where

import Control.Concurrent.STM
import Control.Exception (Exception)
import Control.Monad (filterM, unless, when)
import Data.Map.Strict (Map)
import Data.Map.Strict qualified as Map
import Data.Unique (Unique, newUnique)
import Data.Word (Word64)

-- | One bounded context. Detached t'Operation' handles do not retain it.
data Scheduler = Scheduler !Unique !(TVar State)
data State = State
  { accepting :: !Bool
  , nextKey :: !(Maybe Word64)
  , operations :: !(Map Word64 Operation)
  }

-- | Metadata-only operation identity, readable after responsibility retires.
-- Its owning scope controls advancement and explicit detachment.
data Operation = Operation !Unique !Word64 !Lane !(TVar Status) !(Maybe Group)
  deriving stock (Eq)

instance Show Operation where
  showsPrec precedence (Operation _ key _ _ _) =
    showParen (precedence > 10) (showString "Operation " . shows key)

-- | Opaque metadata identifying one owner's operations. This retains no
-- Runtime, endpoint, resource or scheduler. Groups share admission limits.
newtype Group = Group Unique
  deriving stock (Eq)

-- | Allocate a fresh group without reserving admission or resources.
newGroup :: IO Group
newGroup = Group <$> newUnique

-- | Internal classification. Unknown raw commands belong to 'Waiting'.
-- Mutations serialize until proof or explicit 'detachResponsibility'.
data Lane = Inspection | ScalarRead | Mutation | Waiting
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Last observed progress. Publishing an uncertain 'Outcome' does not
-- advance this stage or establish 'OperationComplete'.
data Stage = Queued | Dispatching | Dispatched | ResponseClosed | OperationComplete
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | First caller result. Later evidence can retire responsibility without
-- rewriting 'OutcomeUnknown' or 'ConnectionRetired'.
data Outcome
  = Succeeded -- ^ Validated successful response and completion proof.
  | Failed -- ^ Validated command failure.
  | NotDispatched -- ^ Proof that the operation was never dispatched.
  | OutcomeUnknown -- ^ Dispatch may have happened; completion remains uncertain.
  | ConnectionRetired -- ^ The connection retired while responsibility remained.
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Progress, published result and responsibility are independent observations.
-- A retained uncertain operation still consumes admission and its lane permit.
data Status = Status
  { stage :: !Stage -- ^ Last proven progress.
  , outcome :: !(Maybe Outcome) -- ^ First published caller result, when available.
  , retained :: !Bool -- ^ Whether the scope still retains logical responsibility.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Operational completion evidence supplied by the Runtime after
-- 'markResponseClosed'. This constructor does not obtain the evidence.
data Completion = Success | CommandFailure
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Rejected admission or transition. 'InvalidTransition' records the
-- required preceding stage followed by the actual stage. No state changes
-- survive a rejected STM action.
data AdmissionError
  = AdmissionClosed
  | AdmissionFull
  | OrdinaryFull
  | KeyExhausted
  | ForeignContext
  | InvalidTransition !Stage !Stage
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)
instance Exception AdmissionError

-- | Create an independent context with 64 admission slots. Ordinary work
-- may occupy 63; inspection can use the remaining capacity. Dispatch allows
-- four waiting jobs, one mutation and four reads, reserving a read permit
-- for inspection. These are selected bounds, not throughput measurements.
newScheduler :: IO Scheduler
newScheduler = Scheduler <$> newUnique <*> newTVarIO (State True (Just 0) Map.empty)

-- | Reserve logical responsibility before dispatch. Saturation or closure
-- throws 'AdmissionError' immediately. Retire queued work with 'cancelQueued';
-- active work requires evidence or explicit 'detachResponsibility'.
admit :: Scheduler -> Lane -> STM Operation
admit scheduler = reserve scheduler Nothing

-- | Reserve an operation in one group, under the scheduler's global limits.
-- Group membership survives logical retirement for physical-owner selection.
-- The token is forced before admission so metadata retains no caller thunk.
admitIn :: Scheduler -> Group -> Lane -> STM Operation
admitIn scheduler group = reserve scheduler (Just group)

reserve :: Scheduler -> Maybe Group -> Lane -> STM Operation
reserve (Scheduler context variable) group lane = do
  case group of
    Just token -> token `seq` pure ()
    Nothing -> pure ()
  current <- readTVar variable
  unless current.accepting (throwSTM AdmissionClosed)
  when (Map.size current.operations >= 64) (throwSTM AdmissionFull)
  let ordinary = Map.size (Map.filter (\(Operation _ _ ownedLane _ _) -> ownedLane /= Inspection) current.operations)
  when (lane /= Inspection && ordinary >= 63) (throwSTM OrdinaryFull)
  key <- maybe (throwSTM KeyExhausted) pure current.nextKey
  observed <- newTVar (Status Queued Nothing True)
  let operation = Operation context key lane observed group
      following = if key == maxBound then Nothing else Just (key + 1)
  writeTVar variable $! current {nextKey = following, operations = Map.insert key operation current.operations}
  pure operation

-- | Read detached metadata without IO, including after 'closeAdmission' or
-- explicit 'detachResponsibility'. This does not inspect tmux.
status :: Operation -> STM Status
status (Operation _ _ _ observed _) = readTVar observed

-- | Observe retained metadata in admission order, including uncertain work.
-- The opaque handles remain bound to this context for explicit detach.
outstanding :: Scheduler -> STM [(Operation, Status)]
outstanding (Scheduler _ variable) = do
  current <- readTVar variable
  mapM (\operation -> (operation,) <$> status operation) (Map.elems current.operations)

-- | Retained logical operations in one group, in admission order. Detached
-- operations remain group members but no longer appear in this list.
outstandingIn :: Scheduler -> Group -> STM [(Operation, Status)]
outstandingIn scheduler group = filter (memberOf group . fst) <$> outstanding scheduler

-- | Match ownership metadata, including after completion or detachment.
-- This does not establish logical or physical liveness.
memberOf :: Group -> Operation -> Bool
memberOf group (Operation _ _ _ _ origin) = origin == Just group

-- | Wait for the first published 'Outcome'. Cancelling this transaction
-- changes neither admission nor responsibility; see 'markUnknown'.
await :: Operation -> STM Outcome
await operation = status operation >>= maybe retry pure . (.outcome)

-- | Claim the oldest eligible queued operation and its lane permit together.
-- Saturated classes do not obstruct eligible inspection. Retry while open
-- without eligible work; return 'Nothing' only after 'closeAdmission'.
claim :: Scheduler -> STM (Maybe Operation)
claim (Scheduler _ variable) = do
  current <- readTVar variable
  if not current.accepting then pure Nothing else do
    entries <- mapM (\operation -> do observed <- status operation; pure (operation, observed)) (Map.elems current.operations)
    let active = [lane | (Operation _ _ lane _ _, observed) <- entries, observed.stage /= Queued]
        count lane = length (filter (== lane) active)
        readCount = count ScalarRead + count Inspection
        eligible lane = length active < 16 && case lane of
          Inspection -> readCount < 4
          ScalarRead -> count ScalarRead < 3 && readCount < 4
          Mutation -> count Mutation < 1
          Waiting -> count Waiting < 4
    choose eligible entries
  where
    choose _ [] = retry
    choose eligible ((operation@(Operation _ _ lane observed _), current) : rest) =
      if current.stage == Queued && eligible lane then do
        writeTVar observed $! current {stage = Dispatching}
        pure (Just operation)
      else choose eligible rest

-- | Record dispatch evidence after 'claim'. Repeating the same transition
-- is harmless; a retired handle stays retired. This supplies no IO evidence.
markDispatched :: Scheduler -> Operation -> STM ()
markDispatched = advance Dispatching Dispatched

-- | Record a closed response after 'markDispatched'. This is distinct from
-- operation completion: only 'finish' can record that stronger evidence.
markResponseClosed :: Scheduler -> Operation -> STM ()
markResponseClosed = advance Dispatched ResponseClosed

-- | Record operation-specific completion after 'markResponseClosed' and
-- release logical responsibility once. Preserve any earlier caller outcome.
-- Physical children and buffers still need their independent cleanup.
finish :: Scheduler -> Operation -> Completion -> STM Bool
finish scheduler operation completion = withLive scheduler operation False $ \current -> do
  requireStage ResponseClosed current
  retire scheduler operation ((publish result current) {stage = OperationComplete})
  where result = case completion of Success -> Succeeded; CommandFailure -> Failed

-- | Publish uncertainty for active work, retaining admission and its permit.
-- Return 'False' if already published or retired. This does not cancel work.
markUnknown :: Scheduler -> Operation -> STM Bool
markUnknown = publishActive OutcomeUnknown

-- | Cancel only queued work, publishing 'NotDispatched' and retiring its
-- admission. Active or previously retired operations return 'False'.
cancelQueued :: Scheduler -> Operation -> STM Bool
cancelQueued scheduler operation = withLive scheduler operation False $ \current ->
  if current.stage == Queued then retire scheduler operation (publish NotDispatched current)
  else pure False

-- | Retire a claimed operation only with proven pre-birth refusal. Preserve
-- earlier uncertainty rather than rewriting its published outcome. This
-- function requires 'Dispatching'; it does not establish non-dispatch itself.
refuseBeforeBirth :: Scheduler -> Operation -> STM Bool
refuseBeforeBirth scheduler operation = withLive scheduler operation False $ \current -> do
  requireStage Dispatching current
  retire scheduler operation (publish NotDispatched current)

-- | Publish connection retirement for active work without releasing debt.
-- A retired endpoint does not prove a server job stopped. Later 'finish',
-- 'refuseBeforeBirth' or explicit 'detachResponsibility' can retire it.
connectionRetired :: Scheduler -> Operation -> STM Bool
connectionRetired = publishActive ConnectionRetired

-- | Explicitly relinquish uncertain logical responsibility. Accept only
-- 'OutcomeUnknown' or 'ConnectionRetired'; otherwise return 'False'. Keep
-- the last stage/outcome, and close no native resource. Detaching a mutation
-- permits the next mutation despite possible continuing external effects.
detachResponsibility :: Scheduler -> Operation -> STM Bool
detachResponsibility scheduler operation = withLive scheduler operation False $ \current ->
  if current.outcome `elem` [Just OutcomeUnknown, Just ConnectionRetired]
    then retire scheduler operation current
    else pure False

-- | Close admission, settle queued work as 'NotDispatched' and return all
-- retained active handles for supervision. Wake blocked 'claim' transactions.
-- Repeated close preserves active debt; it does not release native resources.
closeAdmission :: Scheduler -> STM [Operation]
closeAdmission scheduler@(Scheduler _ variable) = do
  current <- readTVar variable
  writeTVar variable $! current {accepting = False}
  filterM (\operation -> do
    observed <- status operation
    if observed.stage == Queued then cancelQueued scheduler operation >> pure False
    else pure True) (Map.elems current.operations)

withLive :: Scheduler -> Operation -> a -> (Status -> STM a) -> STM a
withLive (Scheduler context variable) (Operation origin key _ observed _) absent action = do
  unless (context == origin) (throwSTM ForeignContext)
  current <- readTVar variable
  if Map.member key current.operations then readTVar observed >>= action
  else pure absent

advance :: Stage -> Stage -> Scheduler -> Operation -> STM ()
advance required target scheduler operation@(Operation _ _ _ observed _) =
  withLive scheduler operation () $ \current ->
    unless (current.stage == target) $ do
      requireStage required current
      writeTVar observed $! current {stage = target}

requireStage :: Stage -> Status -> STM ()
requireStage required current =
  unless (current.stage == required) (throwSTM (InvalidTransition required current.stage))

publish :: Outcome -> Status -> Status
publish result current = case current.outcome of
  -- Force the enum too, so detached metadata cannot retain a caller thunk.
  Nothing -> result `seq` current {outcome = Just result}
  Just _ -> current

publishActive :: Outcome -> Scheduler -> Operation -> STM Bool
publishActive result scheduler operation@(Operation _ _ _ observed _) =
  withLive scheduler operation False $ \current -> do
    when (current.stage == Queued) (throwSTM (InvalidTransition Dispatching Queued))
    case current.outcome of
      Just _ -> pure False
      Nothing -> do
        writeTVar observed $! publish result current
        pure True

retire :: Scheduler -> Operation -> Status -> STM Bool
retire (Scheduler _ variable) (Operation _ key _ observed _) current = do
  context <- readTVar variable
  writeTVar observed $! current {retained = False}
  writeTVar variable $! context {operations = Map.delete key context.operations}
  pure True

internal/LibTmux/Internal/Scope.hs.content:
-- | Exception and recovery policy for an owned Runtime scope.
module LibTmux.Internal.Scope
  ( TmuxException (..), CleanupStatus (..), CleanupRecovery
  , ConfigurationProblem (..), TimeoutKind (..), ObservationProblem (..)
  , CleanupActions (..), customCleanupRecovery, observed
  , runScope, runServerScope, cleanupRecoveries, cleanupFailure, cleanupObservation, inspectCleanup, resumeCleanup
  , awaitCleanup, detachUnresolved, operational
  ) where

import Control.Concurrent.STM (atomically)
import Control.Exception
import Control.Exception.Annotation (ExceptionAnnotation)
import Control.Exception.Context qualified as Context
import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import Data.Maybe (catMaybes, isJust)
import Data.Text (Text)
import LibTmux.Internal.Command (ArgumentError)
import LibTmux.Internal.Graph (GraphError)
import LibTmux.Internal.Process qualified as P
import LibTmux.Internal.Runtime qualified as R
import LibTmux.Internal.Scheduler qualified as S
import LibTmux.Options (OptionError)
import LibTmux.Version qualified as Version

-- | Library operational failures. Context-preserving catching retains any
-- cleanup owners; the original application or cancellation exception keeps
-- its class when the callback itself failed.
data TmuxException
  = ServerClosed -- ^ Admission through the retained Server handle has closed.
  | RuntimeClosed -- ^ Admission through the retained Runtime has closed.
  | InvalidConfiguration !ConfigurationProblem -- ^ Configuration failed before acquisition.
  | InvalidObservation !ObservationProblem -- ^ Acquired metadata failed final validation.
  | PaneCaptureRejected !ByteString -- ^ tmux rejected the selected pane or range.
  | PaneCaptureHookFailed !ByteString -- ^ An after-hook failed following a successful capture.
  | PaneTextTooLarge !Int -- ^ Capture exceeded the requested byte limit.
  | BufferTooLarge !Int -- ^ Named buffer data exceeded the byte limit.
  | EnvironmentReadRejected !ByteString -- ^ tmux refused the exact environment query.
  | EnvironmentReadHookFailed !ByteString -- ^ A hook failed after a completed environment query.
  | InvalidSetting !OptionError -- ^ An option or hook was refused before admission.
  | SettingReadRejected !ByteString -- ^ tmux refused the selected option or hook query.
  | SettingReadHookFailed !ByteString -- ^ An after-hook failed following a successful query.
  | SettingReadTooLarge !Int -- ^ The setting reply exceeded the byte limit.
  | InvalidTarget -- ^ Target belongs to a different connection or an offline fixture.
  | UnsupportedTmuxVersion !Version.VersionError -- ^ Daemon release is older than the supported minimum.
  | IncompatibleTmuxClientProtocol -- ^ The daemon rejected the selected client's older-server protocol. No daemon release was observed.
  | InvalidMutationArgument !ArgumentError -- ^ Invalid command operand; no command was admitted.
  | MutationRejected !ByteString -- ^ tmux rejected the primary command; bounded diagnostic bytes.
  | MutationAppliedWithErrors !ByteString -- ^ The primary command ran, then a command hook failed.
  | MutationTimedOut -- ^ The deadline elapsed; a correlated recovery may retain an unknown outcome.
  | OperationFailed !SomeException -- ^ Synchronous backend failure with its original cause.
  | CleanupFailed !CleanupStatus !(Maybe SomeException) -- ^ Cleanup remained incomplete or its worker could not start.
  deriving stock (Show)
instance Exception TmuxException

-- | Which public setting supplied an invalid deadline.
data TimeoutKind = CaptureTimeout | MutationTimeout | PaneWaitTimeout | OwnedOperationTimeout
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | A caller can correct these failures before trying the operation again.
data ConfigurationProblem
  = TimeoutOutOfRange !TimeoutKind
  | InvalidReadArgument !ArgumentError
  | EmptyPaneWaitText
  | PaneWaitBaselineMismatch
  | PosixPathsRequired
  | ExecutableNotFound
  | InvalidLaunchConfiguration !Text
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | A completed native response failed validation.
data ObservationProblem
  = InvalidSnapshot !GraphError
  | EnvironmentReplyTooLarge !Int
  | EnvironmentEntryMissing
  | OptionReplyTypeMismatch !Text
  | PaneTextInvalidUtf8
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Local observations of the selected physical and logical responsibility.
-- Each inspection returns new metadata; it performs no tmux operation.
data CleanupStatus = CleanupStatus
  { complete :: !Bool -- ^ All physical owners, operation workers and logical responsibility have retired.
  , pendingHandles :: !Int -- ^ Server handles still awaiting physical retirement.
  , pendingReads :: !Int -- ^ Decoder or recovery workers retaining operation envelopes.
  , unresolved :: ![(S.Operation, S.Status)] -- ^ Retained logical operations with their observed status.
  , failures :: ![SomeException] -- ^ Currently observed pin, worker or cleanup-request failures.
  }
  deriving stock (Show)

-- | A physical owner outside the Runtime, with the same public recovery policy.
data CleanupActions = CleanupActions
  { observeCleanup :: !(IO CleanupStatus)
  , requestCleanup :: !(IO CleanupStatus)
  , waitCleanup :: !(IO CleanupStatus)
  , detachCleanup :: !(S.Operation -> IO Bool)
  }

data Target
  = RuntimeTarget !R.Runtime
  | ServerTarget !R.Runtime !R.ServerOwner
  | CustomTarget !CleanupActions

-- | Reachable responsibility after an incomplete or failed scope release.
-- Retaining this value keeps its selected cleanup target and Runtime reachable.
data CleanupRecovery = CleanupRecovery !Target !CleanupStatus !(Maybe SomeException)
instance Show CleanupRecovery where
  show _ = "CleanupRecovery"
instance ExceptionAnnotation CleanupRecovery

customCleanupRecovery :: CleanupActions -> CleanupStatus -> Maybe SomeException -> CleanupRecovery
customCleanupRecovery actions = CleanupRecovery (CustomTarget actions)

-- | Protect one registered owner, including its pin acquisition. Keep the
-- registration handoff masked and restore the action with the outer restore.
runServerScope :: R.Runtime -> R.ServerOwner -> IO a -> IO a
runServerScope runtime owner = runTarget (ServerTarget runtime owner)

runScope :: R.Runtime -> IO a -> IO a
runScope runtime = runTarget (RuntimeTarget runtime)

runTarget :: Target -> IO a -> IO a
runTarget target action = mask $ \restore -> do
  case target of
    RuntimeTarget _ -> pure ()
    CustomTarget _ -> pure ()
    ServerTarget runtime owner -> do
      _ <- atomically (R.inspectServerOwner runtime owner)
      pure ()
  body <- tryWithContext @SomeException (restore action)
  cleanup <- tryWithContext @SomeException (shutdownTarget target)
  case cleanup of
    Right status -> do
      if status.complete then either rethrowIO pure body else do
        let !recovery = CleanupRecovery target status Nothing
        case body of
          Left primary -> rethrowIO (annotated recovery primary)
          Right _ -> rethrowIO (annotated recovery
            (ExceptionWithContext mempty (toException (CleanupFailed status Nothing))))
    Left problem -> do
      status <- inspectTarget target
      let ExceptionWithContext _ cause = problem
          !recovery = CleanupRecovery target status (Just cause)
      case body of
        Left primary -> rethrowIO (annotated recovery primary)
        Right _ -> throwCleanup recovery problem

cleanupRecoveries :: SomeException -> [CleanupRecovery]
cleanupRecoveries = Context.getExceptionAnnotations . someExceptionContext

-- | Exception that interrupted the original cleanup attempt, when there was
-- one. Pending ownership alone need not have an associated exception.
cleanupFailure :: CleanupRecovery -> Maybe SomeException
cleanupFailure (CleanupRecovery _ _ problem) = problem

-- | The cleanup metadata recorded when this recovery owner was attached.
cleanupObservation :: CleanupRecovery -> CleanupStatus
cleanupObservation (CleanupRecovery _ status _) = status

-- | Inspect current owned cleanup and logical uncertainty without tmux IO.
inspectCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> IO CleanupStatus
inspectCleanup (CleanupRecovery target _ _) = inspectTarget target

-- | Retry bounded owned cleanup. An incomplete result retains this owner;
-- the operation does not retry a tmux command or release logical uncertainty.
resumeCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> IO CleanupStatus
resumeCleanup recovery@(CleanupRecovery target _ _) =
  recoverCleanup recovery (shutdownTarget target)

-- | Wait for this target's physical cleanup, then inspect its logical debt.
-- The wait has no deadline.
-- Cancellation or failure preserves an annotated cleanup owner. Use
-- 'resumeCleanup' when the caller requires a bounded attempt.
awaitCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> IO CleanupStatus
awaitCleanup recovery@(CleanupRecovery target _ _) = recoverCleanup recovery (awaitTarget target)

detachUnresolved :: CleanupRecovery -> S.Operation -> IO Bool
detachUnresolved (CleanupRecovery target _ _) operation = case target of
  RuntimeTarget runtime -> atomically (R.detachOperation runtime operation)
  ServerTarget runtime owner -> atomically (R.detachServerOwnerOperation runtime owner operation)
  CustomTarget actions -> actions.detachCleanup operation

annotated :: CleanupRecovery -> ExceptionWithContext SomeException -> ExceptionWithContext SomeException
annotated recovery (ExceptionWithContext context problem) =
  ExceptionWithContext (Context.addExceptionAnnotation recovery context) problem

throwCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> ExceptionWithContext SomeException -> IO a
throwCleanup recovery problem@(ExceptionWithContext context cause) =
  case fromException @SomeAsyncException cause of
    Just _ -> rethrowIO (annotated recovery problem)
    Nothing -> rethrowIO (annotated recovery (ExceptionWithContext context
      (toException (CleanupFailed (cleanupObservation recovery) (Just cause)))))

recoverCleanup :: CleanupRecovery -> IO CleanupStatus -> IO CleanupStatus
recoverCleanup (CleanupRecovery target _ _) action =
  catchNoPropagate action $ \problem@(ExceptionWithContext _ (cause :: SomeException)) -> do
    status <- inspectTarget target
    let !recovery = CleanupRecovery target status (Just cause)
    throwCleanup recovery problem

inspectTarget :: Target -> IO CleanupStatus
inspectTarget (RuntimeTarget runtime) = observed <$> atomically (R.inspect runtime)
inspectTarget (ServerTarget runtime owner) = observed <$> atomically (R.inspectServerOwner runtime owner)
inspectTarget (CustomTarget actions) = actions.observeCleanup

shutdownTarget :: Target -> IO CleanupStatus
shutdownTarget (RuntimeTarget runtime) = observed <$> R.shutdown runtime
shutdownTarget (ServerTarget runtime owner) = observed <$> R.shutdownServerOwner runtime owner
shutdownTarget (CustomTarget actions) = actions.requestCleanup

awaitTarget :: Target -> IO CleanupStatus
awaitTarget target@(RuntimeTarget runtime) = R.awaitCleanup runtime >> inspectTarget target
awaitTarget target@(ServerTarget runtime owner) = R.awaitServerOwnerCleanup runtime owner >> inspectTarget target
awaitTarget (CustomTarget actions) = actions.waitCleanup

observed :: R.Report -> CleanupStatus
observed report =
  let failures = map snd report.closeFailures
        <> [problem | (_, P.PinCleanupFailed problem) <- report.pending]
        <> catMaybes (map snd report.readWorkers)
      complete = null report.pending && null report.readWorkers
        && null report.unresolved && null failures
  in CleanupStatus complete (length report.pending) (length report.readWorkers)
       report.unresolved failures

operational :: IO a -> IO a
operational action = catchNoPropagate action $ \original@(ExceptionWithContext context (problem :: SomeException)) ->
  if isJust (fromException @SomeAsyncException problem) || isJust (fromException @TmuxException problem)
    then rethrowIO original
    else rethrowIO (ExceptionWithContext context (OperationFailed problem))

internal/LibTmux/Internal/TmuxText.hs.content:
-- | Owned tmux label bytes with explicit, fallible UTF-8 conversion.
--
-- 'fromBytes' copies its input, so retaining a label cannot retain a larger
-- transport buffer. 'decodeUtf8' reports invalid encoding without discarding
-- the bytes available through 'toBytes'. These operations perform no IO.
module LibTmux.Internal.TmuxText (TmuxText, fromBytes, toBytes, decodeUtf8) where

import Control.DeepSeq (NFData (rnf))
import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import Data.ByteString.Short (ShortByteString)
import Data.ByteString.Short qualified as Short
import Data.String (IsString (fromString))
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import Data.Text.Encoding qualified as Utf8
import Data.Text.Encoding.Error (UnicodeException)

-- | A lossless reported label. Equality and ordering compare bytes.
-- String literals use UTF-8; byte constructors also admit non-text data.
-- Conversion functions are exposed in "LibTmux.Snapshot".
newtype TmuxText = TmuxText ShortByteString
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)

instance NFData TmuxText where
  rnf (TmuxText bytes) = rnf bytes

instance IsString TmuxText where
  fromString = fromBytes . Utf8.encodeUtf8 . Text.pack

-- | Copy reported bytes into an independently owned label without decoding.
fromBytes :: ByteString -> TmuxText
fromBytes = TmuxText . Short.toShort

-- | Return the exact reported bytes in a strict buffer.
toBytes :: TmuxText -> ByteString
toBytes (TmuxText bytes) = Short.fromShort bytes

-- | Decode as UTF-8; invalid bytes return 'UnicodeException' without replacement.
decodeUtf8 :: TmuxText -> Either UnicodeException Text
decodeUtf8 = Utf8.decodeUtf8' . toBytes

-- and resume retained operations. Typed IDs,

-- | Discover daemon-dependent application operations before creating resources.
-- The table describes the complete Haskell operation, including its required
-- exit observation. The general library admission floor remains separate.
module LibTmux.Capabilities
  ( Capability (..), CapabilityInfo (..), CapabilityHandling (..)
  , Capabilities, CapabilityError (..)
  , capabilitiesFor, daemonVersion, capabilityInfo, capabilityRegistry
  , supports, requireCapability, capabilityManifest
  ) where

import Control.Exception (Exception)
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import Data.Maybe (mapMaybe)
import LibTmux.Version (TmuxVersion, parseVersion)

-- | Individually discoverable daemon operations and command flags.
data Capability
  = ManagedPrograms | ProgramInput | RenderedScreen | ProgramExitEvents | RawBufferPasteFlag
  | ControlNotifications
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Enum, Bounded, Show)

-- | Refuse the operation or use an older native behavior below its floor.
data CapabilityHandling = Refuse | Fallback
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | One canonical feature requirement and its behavior below 'since'.
data CapabilityInfo = CapabilityInfo
  { capability :: !Capability
  , identifier :: !Text
  , since :: !TmuxVersion
  , handling :: !CapabilityHandling
  , apis :: ![Text]
  , commands :: ![Text]
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | A release supplied by the caller, or observed from the pinned daemon by
-- 'LibTmux.Server.serverCapabilities'. A client executable's release is irrelevant.
newtype Capabilities = Capabilities TmuxVersion
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | An unavailable operation and the actual daemon release.
data CapabilityError = CapabilityUnavailable !Capability !TmuxVersion
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)
instance Exception CapabilityError

-- | Evaluate the registry against a supplied version without external effects.
capabilitiesFor :: TmuxVersion -> Capabilities
capabilitiesFor = Capabilities

-- | The release against which these capabilities were evaluated.
daemonVersion :: Capabilities -> TmuxVersion
daemonVersion (Capabilities version) = version

-- | The daemon-dependent requirements read by runtime gates. Program input
-- and screen observation share the program lifetime contract, which requires
-- tmux 3.8 event waits.
capabilityRegistry :: [CapabilityInfo]
capabilityRegistry = map capabilityInfo [minBound .. maxBound]

-- | The authoritative requirement for an operation.
capabilityInfo :: Capability -> CapabilityInfo
capabilityInfo = fst . registryEntry

registryEntry :: Capability -> (CapabilityInfo, Maybe Text)
registryEntry selected = case selected of
  ManagedPrograms -> program "program-execution" ["withProgram", "runProgram", "terminateProgram"] ["new-session", "wait-for -E"]
  ProgramInput -> program "program-input" ["sendProgramInput"] ["send-keys -H", "wait-for -E"]
  RenderedScreen -> program "program-screen" ["readProgramScreen"] ["capture-pane", "save-buffer", "wait-for -E"]
  ProgramExitEvents -> program "program-exit" ["waitProgram", "waitProgramFor"] ["wait-for -E", "pane-died", "window-unlinked", "window-layout-changed"]
  RawBufferPasteFlag -> entry "paste-buffer-no-vis" "3.7" Fallback ["pasteBuffer", "pasteBufferWith"] ["paste-buffer -S"]
  ControlNotifications -> entry "control-notifications" "3.2" Refuse ["withControl"] ["attach-session -f"]
  where
    program key = entry key "3.8" Refuse
    entry key minimumRelease policy publicApis nativeCommands =
      (CapabilityInfo selected key (either (error . show) id (parseVersion minimumRelease)) policy publicApis nativeCommands, Nothing)

-- | Whether this complete operation is available. This is a version check;
-- host process-group support and endpoint liveness are checked separately.
supports :: Capabilities -> Capability -> Bool
supports available selected = daemonVersion available >= (capabilityInfo selected).since

-- | Refuse an unavailable operation without performing external effects.
requireCapability :: Capabilities -> Capability -> Either CapabilityError ()
requireCapability available selected
  | supports available selected = Right ()
  | otherwise = Left (CapabilityUnavailable selected (daemonVersion available))

-- | The shared @libtmux-capabilities/1@ projection of the runtime registry.
-- Its vocabulary currently names none of this port's gated operations, so
-- both claim arrays are empty. 'capabilityRegistry' still reports every
-- Haskell operation and 'supports' checks the connected daemon's release.
-- The unit suite checks the packaged @capabilities.json@ against this value.
capabilityManifest :: Text
capabilityManifest = "{\n  \"schema\": \"libtmux-capabilities/1\",\n  \"port\": \"haskell\",\n"
  <> "  \"floor\": {\"minimum\": \"3.3a\"},\n  \"capabilities\": ["
  <> Text.intercalate ", " shared <> "],\n  \"workarounds\": []\n}\n"
  where
    shared = mapMaybe (snd . registryEntry . (.capability)) capabilityRegistry

-- | Checked creation options, explicit link context and historical identities.
--
-- "LibTmux.Server" executes creation in IO through an existing pinned handle.
-- Start from 'defaultSessionOptions', 'defaultWindowOptions' or
-- 'defaultSplitOptions'; option fields perform no IO.
--
-- A t'CreatedEntities' contains the actual references printed by tmux before
-- after-hooks. It remains usable after the Server closes, but proves neither
-- current liveness nor successful process exec. Acquire a fresh snapshot and
-- use "LibTmux.Snapshot" to observe those identities again.
module LibTmux.Creation
  ( SessionOptions (..), InitialProcess (..), defaultSessionOptions
  , WindowSlot (..), WindowPlacement (..), WindowCollision (..)
  , WindowOptions (..), defaultWindowOptions
  , SplitDirection (..), SplitSize (..), SplitOptions (..), defaultSplitOptions
  , CreatedEntities (session, window, pane, windowIndex, serverPid)
  , CreatedSession, CreatedWindow, CreatedPane
  ) where

import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import Data.List.NonEmpty (NonEmpty)
import Data.Text (Text)
import LibTmux.Internal.Graph (CreatedEntities (..), CreatedSession, SessionRef)
import LibTmux.Snapshot (TmuxText)
import LibTmux.Value (Dimension, WindowIndex)
import System.OsPath.Posix (PosixPath)
import System.OsString.Posix (PosixString)

-- | Initial pane process, retaining tmux's distinct execution modes.
-- A native argv needs at least one argument after the executable because tmux
-- treats a single entry as shell input. 'DirectCommand' encodes that condition.
data InitialProcess
  = DefaultProcess -- ^ Use tmux's configured default-command or default shell.
  | ShellCommand !ByteString -- ^ Native shell-command bytes; an empty split command creates a processless pane.
  | DirectCommand !PosixString !(NonEmpty PosixString) -- ^ Execute the program and argv directly.
  deriving stock (Eq)

-- | Checked when creation is requested. Nothing selects native defaults.
-- Names and paths remain literal through tmux format parsing. Environment and
-- shell/argv bytes retain their native interpretation. Options have no Show
-- instance because command and environment data may contain credentials.
data SessionOptions = SessionOptions
  { name :: !(Maybe Text) -- ^ Literal session name, or tmux's generated name.
  , windowName :: !(Maybe TmuxText) -- ^ Literal initial window label; the daemon validates its bytes.
  , workingDirectory :: !(Maybe PosixPath) -- ^ Initial cwd, relative to the calling client's cwd when relative.
  , environment :: ![(PosixString, PosixString)] -- ^ Session overrides, subject to native environment inheritance.
  , width :: !(Maybe Dimension) -- ^ Requested cells, at most 65535; native status/layout rules still apply.
  , height :: !(Maybe Dimension) -- ^ Requested cells, at most 65535; independent of 'width'.
  , updateEnvironment :: !Bool -- ^ Apply tmux's configured update-environment list from the calling client.
  , process :: !InitialProcess -- ^ Initial process mode, separate from creation completion.
  } deriving stock (Eq)

-- | Detached creation with generated names, native geometry/environment and
-- 'DefaultProcess'. Creation captures the calling client's OS context in IO.
defaultSessionOptions :: SessionOptions
defaultSessionOptions = SessionOptions Nothing Nothing Nothing [] Nothing Nothing True DefaultProcess

-- | An exact session/index position at execution time. The occupant can change
-- after a snapshot; this is context, not an expected-window identity check.
-- 'LibTmux.Server.splitPane' also checks its explicit pane belongs to the
-- window occupying this slot. Indices must fit tmux's signed 32-bit domain.
data WindowSlot = WindowSlot !SessionRef !WindowIndex
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | A session's next free index, an exact slot, or insertion beside a slot.
-- Relative insertion can shift existing indices before later creation fails;
-- failure does not promise rollback. Grouped sessions can share these effects.
-- If a relative slot is vacant, tmux creates at that index without insertion.
-- 'After' refuses index 2147483647 before dispatch: no larger index exists.
data WindowPlacement
  = NextFree !SessionRef -- ^ Let tmux choose a free index from the session's base-index.
  | At !WindowSlot -- ^ Create at the exact index, subject to 'WindowCollision'.
  | Before !WindowSlot -- ^ Insert before this slot's current occupant.
  | After !WindowSlot -- ^ Insert after this slot's current occupant.
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Occupied-slot policy for creation. Replacement removes the old link;
-- other links can keep its physical window alive. Later failure can follow
-- removal. Replacing the selected link can select the new window despite @-d@.
data WindowCollision = RefuseOccupied | ReplaceOccupied
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Window creation through an explicit placement. Names and cwd stay literal;
-- environment and process bytes keep tmux's native interpretation. Geometry
-- comes from the target session. tmux may normalize or reject the name.
-- Options carry no Show instance because launch data can contain credentials.
data WindowOptions = WindowOptions
  { windowLabel :: !(Maybe TmuxText) -- ^ Literal label, or tmux's generated name.
  , windowDirectory :: !(Maybe PosixPath) -- ^ Initial cwd; a relative path uses the caller's cwd.
  , windowEnvironment :: ![(PosixString, PosixString)] -- ^ Overrides for the new pane, not the session environment.
  , selectWindow :: !Bool -- ^ Request selection of the new link in its target session.
  , collision :: !WindowCollision -- ^ Refuse or explicitly remove an occupied destination link.
  , windowProcess :: !InitialProcess -- ^ Initial pane process; completion does not prove exec success.
  } deriving stock (Eq)

-- | Generated name, native geometry/cwd/environment, no selection request,
-- 'RefuseOccupied' and 'DefaultProcess'.
defaultWindowOptions :: WindowOptions
defaultWindowOptions = WindowOptions Nothing Nothing [] False RefuseOccupied DefaultProcess

-- | Orientation of the two resulting panes. 'before' chooses the left or top
-- side for the new pane; otherwise it appears right or below the anchor.
data SplitDirection = LeftRight | TopBottom
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Requested extent of the new pane along the split direction. Cells must fit
-- 2147483647 and percentages must be between 1 and 100. tmux's border and layout
-- constraints determine the actual size; a request can be clamped or refused.
data SplitSize = DefaultSplitSize | SplitCells !Dimension | SplitPercent !Integer
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Split one exact pane through an explicit 'WindowSlot'. The pane must occupy
-- that slot's physical window when tmux executes the request. No active-pane
-- lookup, reuse or replacement occurs. Launch fields follow 'WindowOptions'.
data SplitOptions = SplitOptions
  { direction :: !SplitDirection -- ^ Left/right or top/bottom geometry.
  , size :: !SplitSize -- ^ New pane's requested extent; default is tmux's half split.
  , before :: !Bool -- ^ Put the new pane left or above the anchor.
  , fullWindow :: !Bool -- ^ Span the window across the perpendicular dimension.
  , selectPane :: !Bool -- ^ Request selection of the new pane; independent of session link selection.
  , zoom :: !Bool -- ^ Zoom the window, or keep it zoomed when already zoomed.
  , splitDirectory :: !(Maybe PosixPath) -- ^ Explicit initial cwd, literal through format parsing.
  , splitEnvironment :: ![(PosixString, PosixString)] -- ^ Overrides for the new pane.
  , splitProcess :: !InitialProcess -- ^ Initial pane process, independent of creation completion.
  } deriving stock (Eq)

-- | Split below the exact anchor without selection, full-window or zoom
-- requests. Use tmux's size and launch defaults.
defaultSplitOptions :: SplitOptions
defaultSplitOptions = SplitOptions TopBottom DefaultSplitSize False False False False Nothing [] DefaultProcess

-- | A 'CreatedEntities' receipt from new-window: the window and pane are new;
-- the session and link index identify where tmux created them.
type CreatedWindow = CreatedEntities

-- | A 'CreatedEntities' receipt from split-window: the pane is new; its session,
-- physical window and link index record the exact execution context.
type CreatedPane = CreatedEntities

-- | Named entries in the tmux daemon's global or session environment.
module LibTmux.Environment
  ( EnvironmentScope (..), EnvironmentVisibility (..), EnvironmentEntry (..)
  ) where

import Control.DeepSeq (NFData (rnf))
import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import LibTmux.Snapshot (SessionRef)

-- | Select the table itself. A session lookup does not fall back to global.
data EnvironmentScope = GlobalEnvironment | SessionEnvironment !SessionRef
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Hidden entries are kept in tmux and omitted when it spawns processes.
data EnvironmentVisibility = Visible | Hidden
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

instance NFData EnvironmentVisibility where
  rnf visibility = visibility `seq` ()

-- | Literal bytes or a removal marker. An empty value is present.
-- A removal marker stops an inherited value from reaching a new process.
data EnvironmentEntry
  = EnvironmentValue !EnvironmentVisibility !ByteString
  | EnvironmentRemoved !EnvironmentVisibility
  deriving stock (Eq)

src/LibTmux/Id.hs.content:
-- | Distinct session, physical-window and physical-pane IDs.
--
-- Parsing and rendering are pure. An ID carries no endpoint, server lifetime
-- or liveness evidence. Render an ID for external text; use its numeric
-- accessor when an application needs the mathematical value.
--
-- Start with 'parseSessionId', 'parseWindowId' or 'parsePaneId'. Each type's
-- documentation links its parser and renderer. Contextual numeric indices
-- belong to "LibTmux.Value".
--
-- >>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
-- >>> fmap renderWindowId (parseWindowId "@17")
-- Right "@17"
-- >>> either (const "rejected") renderPaneId (parsePaneId "@17")
-- "rejected"
module LibTmux.Id
  ( -- * Entity identities
    SessionId
  , WindowId
  , PaneId
    -- * Parse external values
  , IdError (..)
  , parseSessionId
  , parseWindowId
  , parsePaneId
    -- * Render target text
  , renderSessionId
  , renderWindowId
  , renderPaneId
    -- * Read numeric values
  , sessionIdValue
  , windowIdValue
  , paneIdValue
  ) where

import Control.DeepSeq (NFData)
import Control.Monad (guard)
import Data.Char (ord)
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import Data.Word (Word32)

-- | A session's unsigned 32-bit tmux identifier, written with a @$@ prefix.
-- Parse with 'parseSessionId'; render with 'renderSessionId'.
newtype SessionId = SessionId Word32
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | A physical window's identifier, independent of its session links.
-- Parse with 'parseWindowId'; render with 'renderWindowId'.
newtype WindowId = WindowId Word32
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | A physical pane's identifier, written with a @%@ prefix.
-- Parse with 'parsePaneId'; render with 'renderPaneId'.
newtype PaneId = PaneId Word32
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | Invalid canonical syntax, entity prefix or native unsigned range.
-- Diagnostics retain at most 64 characters of input.
data IdError = InvalidId
  { expectedPrefix :: !Char -- ^ Required entity prefix.
  , input :: !Text -- ^ Bounded copy of the invalid input.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Parse @$0@ through @$4294967295@. No whitespace or leading zeroes.
parseSessionId :: Text -> Either IdError SessionId
parseSessionId = fmap SessionId . parseId '$'

-- | Parse a canonical @\@number@ identifying a physical window.
parseWindowId :: Text -> Either IdError WindowId
parseWindowId = fmap WindowId . parseId '@'

-- | Parse a canonical @%number@ identifying a physical pane.
parsePaneId :: Text -> Either IdError PaneId
parsePaneId = fmap PaneId . parseId '%'

-- | Render the session prefix and decimal ID.
renderSessionId :: SessionId -> Text
renderSessionId (SessionId value) = "$" <> Text.pack (show value)

-- | Render the physical window prefix and decimal ID.
renderWindowId :: WindowId -> Text
renderWindowId (WindowId value) = "@" <> Text.pack (show value)

-- | Render the physical pane prefix and decimal ID.
renderPaneId :: PaneId -> Text
renderPaneId (PaneId value) = "%" <> Text.pack (show value)

-- | Read the numeric session ID without narrowing conversion.
sessionIdValue :: SessionId -> Integer
sessionIdValue (SessionId value) = toInteger value

-- | Read the numeric physical window ID.
windowIdValue :: WindowId -> Integer
windowIdValue (WindowId value) = toInteger value

-- | Read the numeric physical pane ID.
paneIdValue :: PaneId -> Integer
paneIdValue (PaneId value) = toInteger value

parseId :: Char -> Text -> Either IdError Word32
parseId prefix input = maybe invalid Right parsed
  where
    invalid = Left (InvalidId prefix (Text.copy (Text.take 64 input)))
    parsed = do
      guard (Text.length input <= 11)
      (actual, digits) <- Text.uncons input
      guard (actual == prefix)
      (first, rest) <- Text.uncons digits
      guard (first /= '0' || Text.null rest)
      guard (Text.all (\c -> c >= '0' && c <= '9') digits)
      let value = Text.foldl' (\n c -> n * 10 + toInteger (ord c - ord '0')) 0 digits
      guard (value <= toInteger (maxBound @Word32))
      pure (fromInteger value)

src/LibTmux/Options.hs.content:
-- | Discover options and hooks from tmux's released option tables.
-- Use 'LibTmux.Server.serverCapabilities' for the connected daemon.
module LibTmux.Options
  ( OptionScope (..), OptionKind (..), OptionShape (..)
  , OptionInfo (..), HookInfo (..)
  , knownOptions, lookupOption, knownHooks, lookupHook
  , OptionTarget (..), OptionLookup (..), OptionValue (..), OptionError (..)
  ) where

import Data.Bifunctor (first)
import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import Data.Int (Int64)
import Data.Map.Strict (Map)
import Data.Map.Strict qualified as Map
import Data.Maybe (mapMaybe)
import Data.Text (Text)
import LibTmux.Capabilities (Capabilities, daemonVersion)
import LibTmux.Internal.OptionTable
  ( Definition (..), OptionScope (..), OptionKind (..), OptionShape (..), definitions )
import LibTmux.Snapshot (PaneRef, SessionRef, WindowRef)
import LibTmux.Version (TmuxVersion, parseVersion)

-- | The definition in the selected release. 'optionSince' is the first
-- qualified release of the current availability period.
data OptionInfo = OptionInfo
  { optionName :: !Text
  , optionKind :: !OptionKind
  , optionScopes :: ![OptionScope]
  , optionShape :: !OptionShape
  , optionChoices :: ![Text]
  , optionSince :: !TmuxVersion
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | An event with native command-array storage and its permitted scopes.
data HookInfo = HookInfo
  { hookName :: !Text
  , hookScopes :: ![OptionScope]
  , hookSince :: !TmuxVersion
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | A store selected explicitly for option and hook operations. A window's
-- options belong to the physical window and are shared by all of its links.
-- There is no global pane store. Hooks do not use 'ServerOptions'.
data OptionTarget
  = ServerOptions
  | GlobalSessionOptions
  | SessionOptionsAt !SessionRef
  | GlobalWindowOptions
  | WindowOptionsAt !WindowRef
  | PaneOptionsAt !PaneRef
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Read the selected store, or follow its native inheritance chain.
data OptionLookup = LocalOption | EffectiveOption
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | A scalar value checked against its native definition. Strings are
-- literal bytes. Keys, colours, styles and commands use tmux spelling.
-- Replies contain the spelling tmux reports, which may normalize supplied
-- values. Read values omit a Show instance to avoid logging stored strings.
data OptionValue
  = StringValue !ByteString
  | NumberValue !Int64
  | KeyValue !ByteString
  | ColourValue !ByteString
  | FlagValue !Bool
  | ChoiceValue !Text
  | CommandValue !ByteString
  | StyleValue !ByteString
  | ColourStringValue !ByteString
  deriving stock (Eq)

-- | Refusal before an option or hook command is admitted.
data OptionError
  = UnknownOption !Text
  | ExpectedScalarOption !Text
  | UnknownHook !Text
  | WrongSettingScope !Text !OptionScope
  | WrongOptionKind !Text !OptionKind
  | UnknownOptionChoice !Text
  | InvalidUserOptionName !Text
  | UnqualifiedOptionVersion !TmuxVersion
  | HookIndexOutOfRange
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | List built-in options by name. The catalogue uses the latest pinned
-- release at or below the daemon's version, from 3.3a through 3.8.
knownOptions :: Capabilities -> [OptionInfo]
knownOptions capabilities =
  mapMaybe (lookupOption capabilities) (Map.keys catalogue)

-- | Look up a canonical built-in option name in the selected catalogue.
lookupOption :: Capabilities -> Text -> Maybe OptionInfo
lookupOption capabilities name = case definitionAt capabilities name of
  Just (since, Option kind scopes shape choices) ->
    Just (OptionInfo name kind scopes shape choices since)
  _ -> Nothing

-- | List the known hooks by event name, with the same version selection as
-- 'knownOptions'.
knownHooks :: Capabilities -> [HookInfo]
knownHooks capabilities = mapMaybe (lookupHook capabilities) (Map.keys catalogue)

-- | Look up the event's canonical name. Removed or unknown hooks are absent.
lookupHook :: Capabilities -> Text -> Maybe HookInfo
lookupHook capabilities name = case definitionAt capabilities name of
  Just (since, Hook scopes) -> Just (HookInfo name scopes since)
  _ -> Nothing

type History = [(TmuxVersion, Maybe (TmuxVersion, Definition))]

catalogue :: Map Text History
catalogue = Map.fromList
  [(name, map versioned history) | (name, history) <- definitions]
  where
    versioned (release, entry) = (version release, first version <$> entry)
    version = either (error . show) id . parseVersion

definitionAt :: Capabilities -> Text -> Maybe (TmuxVersion, Definition)
definitionAt capabilities name = do
  history <- Map.lookup name catalogue
  let released = takeWhile ((<= daemonVersion capabilities) . fst) history
  foldl' (\_ (_, definition) -> definition) Nothing released

-- | Pane capture settings and paste newline policy.
module LibTmux.Pane
  ( PaneCaptureOptions (..), defaultPaneCapture
  , PaneRows (..), PaneRendering (..), PasteNewlines (..)
  ) where

-- | A visible screen or an inclusive range relative to the first visible row.
-- Negative offsets address history. tmux clamps the endpoints to its retained
-- rows. Offset zero is the first visible row. Use ordered offsets from
-- -2147483647 through 32767.
data PaneRows
  = VisibleRows
  | RowsBetween !Int !Int
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Capture plain Unicode or retain tmux's ANSI rendition of the cells.
data PaneRendering = PlainText | AnsiStyled
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Limits apply to the UTF-8 bytes before conversion to text. The transport
-- also bounds the complete response, including framing and hook output.
data PaneCaptureOptions = PaneCaptureOptions
  { rows :: !PaneRows
  , rendering :: !PaneRendering
  , byteLimit :: !Int -- ^ Positive byte limit, up to 1 MiB.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | The visible rows in plain Unicode with a 64 KiB limit.
defaultPaneCapture :: PaneCaptureOptions
defaultPaneCapture = PaneCaptureOptions VisibleRows PlainText 65536

-- | Choose how a named buffer's line feeds reach the target pane. Other
-- bytes are preserved when tmux delivers the paste to the pane.
data PasteNewlines = PreserveLineFeeds | LineFeedsToCarriageReturns
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

src/LibTmux/Program.hs.content:
-- | Run terminal applications through an owned scope. Use
-- 'LibTmux.Server.withProgram' for an interactive handle or
-- 'LibTmux.Server.runProgram' for a final result. These operations borrow the
-- selected daemon and own only their new session, application process group,
-- native command clients, pin, buffers and files.
--
-- A scope sends TERM, waits up to 100ms for leader exit, then sends group KILL
-- through a retained Linux pidfd.
-- Completed cleanup proves leader exit and an empty retained process group.
-- Zombies or uninterruptible members may leave a reachable cleanup recovery.
-- Processes that move to another process group/session escape this contract.
-- Linux 6.9 process-group pidfd signaling and a local daemon in the same PID
-- and filesystem namespaces are required. The selected 'bootstrapShell' must
-- provide Bash dynamic descriptors, timed reads and execfail. It defaults to
-- @\/bin\/bash@ and is probed before application creation. The gate has a
-- separate one-second startup lease; 'commandTimeout' bounds each native
-- command. Neither bounds whole startup: 'executionTimeout' bounds owning
-- setup and the callback. Cleanup wakes a blocked gate with an abort claim;
-- the descriptor closes before application exec.
-- The host operation and tmux 3.8 capability are checked before application
-- resources are created.
--
-- Output is a bounded rendered snapshot, not stdout/stderr byte streaming.
-- Controller-process crash recovery, persistent leases, readiness predicates,
-- keep/detach and MCP operations remain unimplemented. Use the scope while its
-- callback runs; detached t'ProgramResult' values survive cleanup.
module LibTmux.Program
  ( Program, ProgramOptions (..), programOptions
  , ProgramExit (..), StartFailure (..), StartPhase (..)
  , ProgramScreen (..), ProgramResult (..), ProgramError (..)
  , sendProgramInput, readProgramScreen, waitProgram, waitProgramFor, terminateProgram
  , ProgramRecovery, ProgramCleanupStatus (..), programRecoveries, programCleanupFailure
  , inspectProgramCleanup, resumeProgramCleanup
  ) where

import LibTmux.Internal.Program

-- | Typed selection over detached tmux observations.
--
-- Build a t'Query' with a source and 'matching', then use 'runQuery' to read
-- an existing t'Snapshot' without IO. 'fetch' explicitly acquires a new
-- snapshot. Ordinary lists and application predicates remain available
-- through "LibTmux.Snapshot"; portable expressions contain no callbacks.
--
-- Import "LibTmux.Query.Fields" qualified for row-prefixed tokens such as
-- @F.paneActive@ and @F.sessionWindowLinks@. They describe captured values;
-- reading them never contacts tmux.
--
-- Query construction, operands and results are finite. Execution validates
-- every declared requirement before filtering, stably ordering and limiting.
-- The default source order and multiplicity come from the supplied snapshot.
-- A result establishes what was observed, not current liveness or a reserved
-- command target. See 'exactlyOne' before selecting an explicit reference.
--
-- >>> exactlyOne [1 :: Integer]
-- Right 1
-- >>> exactlyOne ([] :: [Integer])
-- Left NoMatches
-- >>> atMostOne ([] :: [Integer])
-- Right Nothing
-- >>> atMostOne [1, 2 :: Integer]
-- Left AtLeastTwoMatches
--
module LibTmux.Query
  ( -- * Descriptions
    Field, Expr, Query, Order, ToMany, ToOne, ToOptional
    -- * Ordered sources
  , sessions, windows, panes, windowLinks, paneOccurrences, clients, serverInfo
    -- * Scalar predicates
  , eq, oneOf, contains, ge, gt, le, lt
  , dimensionAtLeast, dimensionAtMost, paneIndexAtLeast, paneIndexAtMost
  , windowIndexAtLeast, windowIndexAtMost
    -- * Logic and relationships
  , allOf, anyOf, not_, some, every, none, related, optionalRelated
    -- * Selection and ordering
  , matching, orderBy, ascending, descending, limit
    -- * Inspect and evaluate
  , QueryRequirements (..), requirements, QueryError (..), runQuery, fetch
    -- * Cardinality
  , CardinalityError (..), exactlyOne, atMostOne
  ) where

import LibTmux.Internal.Field (Field)
import LibTmux.Internal.Query
  ( Expr, Query, Order, ToMany, ToOne, ToOptional
  , sessions, windows, panes, windowLinks, paneOccurrences, clients, serverInfo
  , eq, oneOf, contains, ge, gt, le, lt
  , dimensionAtLeast, dimensionAtMost, paneIndexAtLeast, paneIndexAtMost
  , windowIndexAtLeast, windowIndexAtMost
  , allOf, anyOf, not_, some, every, none, related, optionalRelated
  , matching, orderBy, ascending, descending, limit
  , QueryRequirements (..), requirements, QueryError (..)
  , CardinalityError (..), exactlyOne, atMostOne
  )
import LibTmux.Internal.Query qualified as Q
import LibTmux.Server (Server)
import LibTmux.Server qualified as Server
import LibTmux.Snapshot (Snapshot)

-- | Validate and evaluate against the supplied complete snapshot. Every
-- requirement is checked before reading rows, including empty sources and
-- zero limits. Consuming a successful result performs only pure processing
-- of owned observations. No acquisition, pushdown or refresh occurs.
runQuery :: Snapshot -> Query row -> Either QueryError [row]
runQuery = Q.runQuery

-- | Acquire a complete fresh snapshot and evaluate the query against it.
-- Compiled evaluator support is checked before IO; version requirements are
-- checked against acquired server metadata. Operational failures propagate
-- as exceptions from 'LibTmux.Server.capture'; use 'LibTmux.Server.tryTmux' to retain their
-- context and recovery owners. Cancellation propagates unchanged.
--
-- This performs one acquisition per call, even when the query is reused or
-- has a zero limit. Use 'runQuery' to reuse an existing t'Snapshot'. No filter
-- is pushed into tmux in this implementation.
fetch :: Server -> Query row -> IO (Either QueryError [row])
fetch server query = case Q.prepare Q.nativeProfile query of
  Left problem -> pure (Left problem)
  Right () -> (`runQuery` query) <$> Server.capture server

-- | Captured fields and relationships for "LibTmux.Query".
--
-- Import this module qualified, for example as @F@. Row prefixes identify
-- the source row in @F.paneActive@ and @F.linkActive@.
-- Tokens describe the tmux 3.3a baseline and never contact tmux. Byte-bearing
-- names and paths, optional values and contextual relationships keep the
-- meanings of "LibTmux.Snapshot".
--
-- >>> LibTmux.Query.requirements (LibTmux.Query.matching (LibTmux.Query.eq paneActive True) LibTmux.Query.panes)
-- QueryRequirements {sourceName = "panes", fieldNames = ["pane.active"], relationshipNames = [], orderingFields = [], rowLimit = Nothing}
module LibTmux.Query.Fields
  ( -- * Sessions
    sessionId, sessionName, sessionAttached, sessionGroup, sessionWindowLinks,
    sessionClients
    -- * Physical windows
  , windowId, windowName, windowWidth, windowHeight, windowLayout, windowZoomed,
    windowPanes, windowLinks
    -- * Physical panes
  , paneId, paneWindowId, paneIndex, paneWidth, paneHeight, paneActive, paneDead,
    paneTitle, paneCurrentCommand, paneCurrentPath, paneCursorX, paneCursorY,
    paneModeCount, paneMode, paneWindow
    -- * Window links
  , linkSessionId, linkWindowId, linkIndex, linkActive, linkFlags, linkSession,
    linkWindow, linkPanes
    -- * Pane occurrences
  , occurrencePane, occurrenceLink
    -- * Clients
  , clientName, clientPid, clientTty, clientWidth, clientHeight, clientAttachment
    -- * Client attachments
  , clientAttachmentSessionId, clientAttachmentWindowId, clientAttachmentWindowIndex,
    clientAttachmentPaneId, clientAttachmentSession, clientAttachmentWindow,
    clientAttachmentPane
    -- * Daemon metadata
  , serverInfoPid, serverInfoStartedAt, serverInfoVersion, serverInfoSocketPath
  ) where

import Data.Text (Text)
import LibTmux.Id (SessionId, WindowId, PaneId)
import LibTmux.Internal.Field qualified as F
import LibTmux.Internal.Query qualified as Q
import LibTmux.Query (Field, ToMany, ToOne, ToOptional)
import LibTmux.Snapshot
  ( Session, Window, Pane, WindowLink, PaneOccurrence, Client, ClientAttachment
  , ServerInfo, TmuxText
  )
import LibTmux.Value (Dimension, PaneIndex, WindowIndex)
import LibTmux.Version (TmuxVersion)
import System.OsPath.Posix (PosixPath)
import System.OsString.Posix (PosixString)

-- | Native session ID without a connection-generation guarantee.
sessionId :: Field Session SessionId
sessionId = F.SessionId

-- | Captured UTF-8 session name. Equality does not normalize Unicode.
sessionName :: Field Session Text
sessionName = F.SessionName

-- | Nonnegative count of attached clients as observed by tmux.
sessionAttached :: Field Session Integer
sessionAttached = F.SessionAttached

-- | Lossless reported group label, or 'Nothing' for an ungrouped session.
sessionGroup :: Field Session (Maybe TmuxText)
sessionGroup = F.SessionGroup

-- | Every window link owned by this session, retaining index and multiplicity.
sessionWindowLinks :: ToMany Session WindowLink
sessionWindowLinks = Q.SessionLinks

-- | Captured clients attached to this session; an empty list is known absence.
sessionClients :: ToMany Session Client
sessionClients = Q.SessionClients

-- | Native physical window ID, independent of a session's link index.
windowId :: Field Window WindowId
windowId = F.WindowId

-- | Lossless window label. Equality and ordering compare its retained bytes.
windowName :: Field Window TmuxText
windowName = F.WindowName

-- | Positive physical window width in cells.
windowWidth :: Field Window Dimension
windowWidth = F.WindowWidth

-- | Positive physical window height in cells.
windowHeight :: Field Window Dimension
windowHeight = F.WindowHeight

-- | Native unzoomed layout encoding, possibly including pane selections.
-- Treat it as opaque, release-dependent text.
windowLayout :: Field Window Text
windowLayout = F.WindowLayout

-- | Whether a pane currently occupies the window through zoom.
windowZoomed :: Field Window Bool
windowZoomed = F.WindowZoomed

-- | Physical panes in this window, ordered by pane index.
windowPanes :: ToMany Window Pane
windowPanes = Q.WindowPanes

-- | All contextual appearances of this window across captured sessions.
windowLinks :: ToMany Window WindowLink
windowLinks = Q.WindowLinks

-- | Native pane ID. Equality alone does not establish Server identity.
paneId :: Field Pane PaneId
paneId = F.PaneId

-- | Native ID of the pane's physical window; use 'paneWindow' to navigate it.
paneWindowId :: Field Pane WindowId
paneWindowId = F.PaneWindow

-- | Pane index within its window, distinct from a window-link index.
paneIndex :: Field Pane PaneIndex
paneIndex = F.PaneIndex

-- | Positive width in cells. Use 'LibTmux.Query.dimensionAtLeast' for an integer threshold.
paneWidth :: Field Pane Dimension
paneWidth = F.PaneWidth

-- | Positive height in cells, independent of window-link context.
paneHeight :: Field Pane Dimension
paneHeight = F.PaneHeight

-- | Whether this is the active pane of its physical window.
paneActive :: Field Pane Bool
paneActive = F.PaneActive

-- | Whether tmux observed the pane's process as dead.
paneDead :: Field Pane Bool
paneDead = F.PaneDead

-- | UTF-8 pane title. 'LibTmux.Query.contains' performs exact Text substring matching.
paneTitle :: Field Pane Text
paneTitle = F.PaneTitle

-- | Foreground command name as lossless POSIX bytes, not a shell command line.
paneCurrentCommand :: Field Pane PosixString
paneCurrentCommand = F.PaneCommand

-- | Observed current directory on the tmux endpoint, preserving POSIX bytes.
paneCurrentPath :: Field Pane PosixPath
paneCurrentPath = F.PanePath

-- | Zero-based base-screen column; may equal width when a wrap is pending.
paneCursorX :: Field Pane Integer
paneCursorX = F.PaneCursorX

-- | Zero-based base-screen row, independent of the current mode's cursor.
paneCursorY :: Field Pane Integer
paneCursorY = F.PaneCursorY

-- | Native pane mode-stack depth, including zero.
paneModeCount :: Field Pane Integer
paneModeCount = F.PaneModeCount

-- | Current mode name, or 'Nothing' when no mode is active.
paneMode :: Field Pane (Maybe Text)
paneMode = F.PaneMode

-- | Resolve the pane's physical window in the supplied snapshot with 'LibTmux.Query.related'.
paneWindow :: ToOne Pane Window

-- | Recover incomplete operations and scope cleanup using the exception
-- context returned by "LibTmux.Server" or by `tryWithContext`.
-- Inspection reads retained metadata. Resuming cleanup never submits
-- the original command again.
module LibTmux.Recovery
  ( -- * Scope cleanup
    CleanupRecovery, CleanupStatus (..), cleanupRecoveries, cleanupFailure, cleanupObservation
  , inspectCleanup, resumeCleanup, awaitCleanup, detachUnresolved
    -- * Capture
  , CaptureRecovery, captureRecoveries, recoveryOperation, recoveryGeneration
  , ReadRecovery (..), inspectCaptureRecovery, resumeCaptureRecovery, detachCaptureRecovery
    -- * Creation
  , CreationRecovery, creationRecoveries, creationOperation, creationGeneration
  , creationReceipt, inspectCreationRecovery, resumeCreationRecovery, awaitCreationRecovery, detachCreationRecovery
    -- * Mutation
  , MutationRecovery, mutationRecoveries, mutationOperation, mutationGeneration
  , inspectMutationRecovery, resumeMutationRecovery, awaitMutationRecovery, detachMutationRecovery
    -- * Program cleanup
  , ProgramRecovery, ProgramCleanupStatus (..), programRecoveries, programCleanupFailure
  , inspectProgramCleanup, resumeProgramCleanup
    -- * Control client cleanup
  , ControlRecovery, controlRecoveries, controlRetired, resumeControlCleanup
    -- * Operation metadata
  , Operation, Status (..), Stage (..), Outcome (..), operationStatus
  ) where

import Control.Concurrent.STM (atomically)
import Control.Exception.Context (ExceptionContext, getExceptionAnnotations)
import LibTmux.Creation qualified as Creation
import LibTmux.Internal.Capture (CaptureRecovery)
import LibTmux.Internal.Capture qualified as C
import LibTmux.Internal.Control (ControlRecovery, controlRecoveries, controlRetired, resumeControlCleanup)
import LibTmux.Internal.Creation (CreationRecovery)
import LibTmux.Internal.Creation qualified as Create
import LibTmux.Internal.Mutation (MutationRecovery)
import LibTmux.Internal.Mutation qualified as M
import LibTmux.Internal.Runtime (ReadRecovery (..))
import LibTmux.Internal.Runtime qualified as R
import LibTmux.Internal.Scheduler (Operation, Status (..), Stage (..), Outcome (..))
import LibTmux.Internal.Scheduler qualified as S
import LibTmux.Internal.Scope
  ( CleanupRecovery, CleanupStatus (..), cleanupFailure, cleanupObservation
  , inspectCleanup, resumeCleanup, awaitCleanup, operational
  )
import LibTmux.Internal.Scope qualified as Scope
import LibTmux.Program
  ( ProgramRecovery, ProgramCleanupStatus (..), programRecoveries, programCleanupFailure
  , inspectProgramCleanup, resumeProgramCleanup
  )
import LibTmux.Snapshot (Generation)

-- | Correlated creation owners from 'LibTmux.Server.tryTmux' or 'tryWithContext'. Keep the
-- context when handling failure, including an applied command's hook error.
creationRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [CreationRecovery]
creationRecoveries = getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Metadata-only identity of the original creation operation.
creationOperation :: CreationRecovery -> Operation
creationOperation = R.receiptOperation . Create.recoveryReceipt

-- | Originating Server generation, including after the scope closes.
creationGeneration :: CreationRecovery -> Generation
creationGeneration = R.receiptGeneration . Create.recoveryReceipt

-- | Read any complete historical receipt already observed by the library.
-- This reads owned metadata without contacting tmux. 'Nothing' does not mean
-- no entity was created; unread or incomplete evidence cannot supply IDs.
creationReceipt :: CreationRecovery -> IO (Maybe Creation.CreatedEntities)
creationReceipt = atomically . Create.observedReceipt

-- | Inspect logical outcome and native ownership without external operations.
inspectCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
inspectCreationRecovery = atomically . Create.inspectRecovery

-- | Resume existing cleanup; never execute the creation again.
resumeCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO ()
resumeCreationRecovery = operational . Create.resumeRecovery

-- | Join the original native child and decoder. Logical uncertainty can
-- remain, and this wait proves no hook/background-job completion.
awaitCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
awaitCreationRecovery = operational . Create.awaitRecovery

-- | Relinquish logical uncertainty while preserving physical cleanup owners.
-- This does not remove the created session or repeat the command.
detachCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO Bool
detachCreationRecovery = operational . atomically . Create.detachRecovery

-- | Cleanup owners retained by a failed or cancelled scope. The context
-- comes from 'LibTmux.Server.tryTmux' or 'tryWithContext'. Inspection performs no tmux IO.
-- Nested scopes can contribute overlapping owners; inspect and resume each
-- retained responsibility through 'inspectCleanup' and 'resumeCleanup'.
cleanupRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [CleanupRecovery]
cleanupRecoveries = getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Relinquish one logical operation from this cleanup scope. This releases
-- no native resources and does not prove that daemon-side work completed.
detachUnresolved :: CleanupRecovery -> Operation -> IO Bool
detachUnresolved recovery = operational . Scope.detachUnresolved recovery

-- | Read owners retained by a capture or Server version check, including cancellation.
captureRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [CaptureRecovery]
captureRecoveries = getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Metadata-only operation identity for the failed capture.
recoveryOperation :: CaptureRecovery -> Operation
recoveryOperation = R.receiptOperation . C.recoveryReceipt

-- | Correlate the failed capture with its Server generation.
recoveryGeneration :: CaptureRecovery -> Generation
recoveryGeneration = R.receiptGeneration . C.recoveryReceipt

-- | Observe logical outcome, decoder ownership and native cleanup locally.
-- This reads runtime metadata and performs no tmux command.
inspectCaptureRecovery :: CaptureRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
inspectCaptureRecovery = atomically . C.inspectRecovery

-- | Resume existing cleanup without dispatching the capture again.
resumeCaptureRecovery :: CaptureRecovery -> IO ()
resumeCaptureRecovery = operational . C.resumeRecovery

-- | Explicitly detach logical uncertainty while preserving native ownership.
detachCaptureRecovery :: CaptureRecovery -> IO Bool
detachCaptureRecovery = operational . atomically . C.detachRecovery

-- | Recover the exact operation after failure, timeout or cancellation. The
-- context comes from 'LibTmux.Server.tryTmux' or 'tryWithContext'; cancellation keeps its
-- original exception class and is not caught by 'LibTmux.Server.tryTmux'.
mutationRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [MutationRecovery]
mutationRecoveries = getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Metadata-only identity of the original command. 'operationStatus' remains
-- available after native cleanup; this value contains no command operands.
mutationOperation :: MutationRecovery -> Operation
mutationOperation = R.receiptOperation . M.recoveryReceipt

-- | Server generation associated with this mutation's recovery owner.
mutationGeneration :: MutationRecovery -> Generation
mutationGeneration = R.receiptGeneration . M.recoveryReceipt

-- | Inspect the original operation's logical and physical ownership locally.
-- This performs no tmux command. An unknown outcome does not become success
-- merely because the native child has exited.
inspectMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
inspectMutationRecovery = atomically . M.inspectRecovery

-- | Resume existing native cleanup and decoder ownership, without repeating
-- the command. Allocation failure retains the same recovery owner.
resumeMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO ()
resumeMutationRecovery = operational . M.resumeRecovery

-- | Wait for the original decoder and native child to retire. This may still
-- return retained 'OutcomeUnknown'; it does not wait for a daemon hook job.
-- Cancellation keeps this recovery owner in the new exception context.
awaitMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
awaitMutationRecovery = operational . M.awaitRecovery

-- | Relinquish this operation's logical uncertainty. This neither cancels
-- daemon work nor releases native resources, and never repeats the mutation.
detachMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO Bool
detachMutationRecovery = operational . atomically . M.detachRecovery

-- | Read retained operation metadata, including after its physical cleanup.
operationStatus :: Operation -> IO Status
operationStatus = atomically . S.status

-- | Start, observe and change a tmux daemon through a scoped handle.
--
-- A t'Server' represents one adoption of one endpoint. 'withOwnedServer'
-- starts and retires a private daemon. 'withServer' borrows a daemon and
-- releases its socket pin, native command clients and cleanup workers when
-- the scope closes. The tmux noun @Client@ refers to detached observations in
-- "LibTmux.Snapshot".
-- 'withRuntime' and 'withServerIn' give several handles shared resource limits
-- and independent Server scopes.
--
-- 'capture' returns fully decoded, validated values. Field access and graph
-- navigation are pure. Captures use an observation interval, not an atomic
-- transaction over tmux and operating-system state.
-- 'createSession', 'createWindow' and 'splitPane' return historical identities.
-- 'renameSession',
-- 'renameWindow' and 'setPaneTitle' update generation-bound targets.
-- 'killServer', 'killSession', 'killWindow' and 'killPane' retire their targets.
-- Capture again to observe their effects.
--
-- Operational failures use t'TmuxException'. 'tryTmux' catches that type only.
-- Cancellation and callback failures keep their original exception class.
-- Use "LibTmux.Recovery" to inspect retained owners after incomplete cleanup.
module LibTmux.Server
  ( -- * Open and observe
    Server, ServerConfig (..), serverConfig, withServer, capture, serverGeneration, serverCapabilities
  , withControl
  , OwnedServerConfig (..), defaultOwnedServerConfig, withOwnedServer
    -- * Mutation deadlines
  , MutationOptions (..), defaultMutationOptions
    -- * Session, window and pane creation
  , createSession, createSessionWith
  , createWindow, createWindowWith, splitPane, splitPaneWith
    -- * Owned terminal applications
  , withProgram, runProgram
    -- * Rename and title
  , renameSession, renameSessionWith, renameWindow, renameWindowWith, setPaneTitle, setPaneTitleWith
    -- * Environment
  , getEnvironment, setEnvironment, setEnvironmentWith
  , markEnvironmentRemoved, markEnvironmentRemovedWith, unsetEnvironment, unsetEnvironmentWith
    -- * Option and hook stores
  , readOption, setOption, setOptionWith, unsetOption, unsetOptionWith
  , readHook, setHook, setHookWith, unsetHook, unsetHookWith
    -- * Window links, selection and layout
  , linkWindow, linkWindowWith, unlinkWindow, unlinkWindowWith
  , selectWindowLink, selectWindowLinkWith, selectExactPane, selectExactPaneWith
  , NamedLayout (..), selectLayout, selectLayoutWith
    -- * Absolute geometry
  , resizePane, resizePaneWith, resizeWindow, resizeWindowWith
    -- * Remove a target
  , killServer, killSession, killSessionWith, killWindow, killWindowWith, killPane, killPaneWith
    -- * Named paste buffers
  , loadBuffer, loadBufferWith, readBuffer, pasteBuffer, pasteBufferWith
    -- * Pane input
  , PaneInput (..), sendKeys, sendKeysWith
    -- * Pane text
  , PaneText, capturePane, paneText
  , PaneWaitOptions (..), defaultPaneWait, PaneMatch (..), PaneWaitResult (..), waitForText
    -- * Shared ownership
  , Runtime, withRuntime, withServerIn
    -- * Operational failures
  , TmuxException (..), ConfigurationProblem (..), TimeoutKind (..), ObservationProblem (..)
  , ArgumentError (..), tryTmux
  ) where

  ( TmuxException (..), ConfigurationProblem (..), TimeoutKind (..), ObservationProblem (..), operational )
import LibTmux.Internal.Scope qualified as Scope
import LibTmux.Internal.SocketPin qualified as Pin
import LibTmux.Options
  ( HookInfo (..), OptionError (..), OptionInfo (..), OptionKind (..)
  , OptionLookup (..), OptionScope (..), OptionShape (..), OptionTarget (..), OptionValue (..)
  )
import LibTmux.Options qualified as Options
import LibTmux.Pane (PaneCaptureOptions (..), PasteNewlines, defaultPaneCapture)
